Someone asked how and why someone would "paint" their gun. Well many reasons. One is that is personalizes the firearm to you. Make it what you want and how you feel it should appear.

It also protects the parts from rusting, or corrosion. Not to mention scratches. That adonized shit scratches very very easy I have found. With duracoat you really have to work hard to blemish it once cured.

So now that we got the benefits out of the way why duracoat as to cerakote? Well that is the easiest to answer. Duracoat doesn't need to be heated to be cured, and many firearms I have seen that were professional done still had rust build up under the coat. Moisture got locked under the coating and just sealed it in there.

With duracoat it pulls the moisture away and hey I don't know the science, but I know it works.

So first thing first. Get your weapon taken apart, and I mean everything out of it because with a firearm precision is everything and over spray does happen. Last thing you want is a malfunction. So once apart go to this site and check it out. I suggest ordering from them direct because sales are often and even with their shipping cost it is still cheaper and easier to get it this way.

Now they say one can will do 2 firearms......no it won't. With my FDE I used two cans and the hand guard only got two coats. Three is best. So keep that in mind before you go about this.

Next you will need a scotch bright pad. Those abrasive green pads for dishes? You want to scrub the hell out of every piece. Can't use duracoat on rubber so use that as accent pieces. Once you have done that and can see it lose it's sheen you are ready for step two.

Degreaser on all of the pieces you want to paint. I used purple power from Walmart. You coat it really good and let sit for 30 min in the hot sun. This gets all the oils and stuff out of the metal. Oh make sure you wear gloves at this point. You don't want the oil from your hands on the surface.

After it has been there for a while change gloves and rinse each piece with brake clean. Don't be shy either. Really get that shit off. Allow those pieces to dry and you will see white residue on adonized parts. It is ok too.

When applying the paint make sure to be far enough away to eliminate runs and do even coats. Let dry overnight and assemble the weapon after 12 hours. Light use for another 12 hrs and then it is good.
